🚨🇲🇽 <u>419 to 0: Mexico's Deputies Vote Prison for Cartel Recruitment</u>

Every party in Mexico's Chamber of Deputies backed making forced recruitment by organized crime a crime of its own: 10 to 20 years in prison, rising to 15 to 25 when there are threats, coercion or violence. Any recruitment of children and teenagers counts as forced, whatever the means. The bill now goes to the Senate. It's the same day the security cabinet reported taking down 800 recruitment accounts on social media.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>"Free Medicine" Stamped on Every Box: Mexico Goes After Stolen Drugs</u>

Medicines handed out free in public hospitals keep turning up for sale in tianguis and private pharmacies, sometimes right outside the clinic gate. Deputy Health Secretary Eduardo Clark says packaging now carries the label "La salud es un derecho, medicamento gratuito," and a digital tracking system will follow every lot to the unit it was sent to, and for high-cost treatments to the patient. Some of those boxes cost over 200,000 pesos each. If you see one for sale, report it.
banner: STOLEN MEDICINE: EVERY BOX NOW TRACKED

text:
🇲🇽🌳 <u>Profepa Shuts Down Illegal Resort in Tepozteco National Park</u>

Mexico's environmental prosecutor Profepa ordered a total temporary closure of "Vyda Tepoztlán," a cabin-and-pool tourist complex going up without an environmental permit inside El Tepozteco National Park, in the Indigenous community of Amatlán de Quetzalcóatl, right next to the Poza Sagrada. A citizen complaint triggered the October 15 inspection with the National Guard and the Army. The site sits in the Bosque de Agua, which recharges the aquifers that supply Morelos. The developer now faces sanctions and must restore the land.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Maya Communities: Pig Megafarms Are Fouling Yucatán's Cenotes</u>

A Greenpeace study of 17 wells and cenotes across seven Yucatán towns, including Kinchil, Sitilpech, Celestún and Chocholá, found harmful bacteria, excess nitrates and porcine fecal indicators. A year after the Maya network To'one Ja'o'on filed a formal complaint with federal authorities, the Kekén complexes near Kinchil and Celestún are still operating. The communities say they aren't asking for new promises. They want inspections, results and repair of the damage, plus a halt to new permits and expansions.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Heart Attack? Your Insurance Status No Longer Matters</u>

Mexico's Universal Health Service will treat acute heart attacks at the nearest capable public unit, whether the patient is covered by IMSS, ISSSTE or nobody at all. Starting in 2027, a national rapid-response protocol puts saving the patient ahead of paperwork. Built on the National Cardiology Institute's Código Infarto, it routes patients straight to angioplasty or clot-busting therapy. No more being turned away at the door for carrying the wrong card.
banner: HEART ATTACK CARE: NO INSURANCE NEEDED

text: 🇲🇽🌎 "We cannot negotiate anything outside our Constitution, our laws, or anything we know will hurt the national economy or jobs." "We very firmly defend the Mexicans in the United States. That is our first defense, above all." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 20, 2026 Asked about Trump saying a trade deal is very close, Sheinbaum said "we are already very close," but some issues remain. Mexico's goal is to cut the US tariffs on vehicles and steel as far as possible, with no new tariffs. Every agreement follows four principles: sovereignty, territorial integrity, mutual trust and "coordination without subordination." She cited a new mirror operation on the border, with each country's army on its own side, and said Mexican authorities have arrested five of the FBI's ten most wanted in Mexico.

🔥🇲🇽 "The people's judgment is enough on a person dedicated to politics who calls on a foreign government to intervene in Mexico." "I don't believe any Mexican agrees that the decisions of the people of Mexico be made abroad." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 20, 2026 A reporter asked whether the Attorney General should open treason cases against PRI leader Alejandro Moreno, who wrote to Marco Rubio asking Washington to apply a US law against Mexico's electoral councillors, and PAN senator Lilly Téllez, who the reporter said called on Fox News for an armed US intervention. Sheinbaum said no. Former Chihuahua prosecutor César Jáuregui faces treason charges for violating the National Security Law by bringing US agents into a ground operation; a political statement is different. "Justice is above even politics." Let the people judge: about 80% of Mexicans reject those attitudes.

🔥🇲🇽 "If there was a government that was linked to the narco, it was Calderón's, with his security secretary arrested. [...] A people that has no memory has no compass." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 20, 2026 The PAN's national president now says governments linked to drug trafficking commit treason. "Well, and García Luna and the PAN governments?" Sheinbaum answered. Genaro García Luna, Felipe Calderón's security secretary from 2006 to 2012, was convicted in the US of taking cartel bribes. She said she has asked the Finance Ministry for the Fobaproa files, the 1990s bank bailout that turned private debt into public debt, to document cases like the Autopista del Sol and Salinas y Rocha rescues. She also recalled the "Estafa Maestra" and Pemex's purchase of the Agronitrogenados scrap plant. "Those criticizing us have forgotten how they watered down cancer medicines."
banner: "A PEOPLE WITHOUT MEMORY HAS NO COMPASS"
